info.title: Attome XRM API
info.description: The Attome XRM platform's HTTP API. Entity record shapes under `/api/v1/{entity}` are resolved from each deployment's runtime metadata (D-003) and therefore cannot be enumerated statically — those operations document the generic envelope only. Fetch `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields.

contract so the OpenAPI document and the Angular client exist before the
executor is wired to the fused statement — the handler currently validates,
routes, and reports, which is the half that has a testable contract.

post.summary: Find passages or images like a record, file, description or image
post.description:
Embeds the record's text, the document's file text or the description and returns the nearest
record passages the caller may read: records' long fields and, for entities whose search setting
turns document embeddings on, the text of the files attached to them, with the page of a PDF.
With an image-text model configured, an `image`, or `images: true` with a description or a
document, returns the nearest images instead (documents attached to records of entities whose
search setting turns image embeddings on), each named by its document.

200.description: The nearest readable passages, nearest first

404.description: The record or document does not exist or is not readable

422.description: Not exactly one source, or a source with no text

503.description: No embedding model (or no image-text model for an image search), or semantic search switched off

x-audit-exempt.note: a bounded, permission-filtered nearest-passage search; persists nothing

AskResult.description: What asking did, beside the results.

answer.description: For a question: `{answer, citations}` or `{answer: null, reason}`.

filter.description: The filter the words became: `{entity, where}`, the `query/run` form.

reason.description: Why there is no filter, when declined.

status.description: `parsed` (the filter ran) or `declined` (a plain search ran).

searches.description: Searches whose results showed this entity.

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `customer_tests_failed`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`request_rejected`, `invalid_cursor`, `resync_needed`, `cascade_restricted`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

errors.description:
Every field-level failure on a `validation_error`, as
`{attribute, rule, message, fix}`.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

instance.description: The request path the problem happened at.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

retryable.description:
Whether the same request may succeed later (the error catalogue's
verdict for `code`).

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

title.description:
A short title for `code` in the request's language (Z14-T3), e.g.
`The resource was not found.`

type.description: Z14-T1 (RFC 9457): `about:blank`; the problem is named by `code`.

ExplainedPassage.description: One retrieved passage and the terms that brought it.

matched_terms.description: Terms found in the title, headings or passage.

FacetCount.description: One facet value and how many results have it.

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

GapTopic.description:
A row of the authors' knowledge-gap queue (D-452; surfaced by D-489).

The phrase is the scrubbed topic, never the caller's raw question — read
[`normalize_gap_phrase`]'s doc before widening anything here, and D-452
before changing what a row stores.

addressed_item_ref.description:
The Knowledge Base item that addressed this gap (D-489, migration
0300). No FK: the target is a runtime-provisioned entity table.

addressed_page_ref.description: The content page that addressed this gap, from the 0263 shape.

edge_type.description:
`"lookup:{field}"`, `"hierarchy:{field}"`, or `"relationship:{type}"`
— typed by source, per the plan's response contract.

IndexSize.description: A25-T5: one entity's share of the search index, as last measured.

IndexerStatus.description: The indexer's own state, shared by every collection.

drain_last_advanced_at.description:
When the search drain last advanced its cursor over the change feed —
the last time it processed any entity write, knowledge or not (or,
before its first event, when it first started). `None` when no drain
has ever started.

embedding_model.description:
The model chunk vectors are written with, or `None` when knowledge is
lexical-only by configuration.

KnowledgeExplanation.description:
Why a retrieval returned what it did, for an administrator (roadmap
N15-T4): the terms the question was reduced to, the words dropped as
function words, and for each passage, in rank order, which terms it
matched. Retrieved under the administrator's own permissions, lexical
mode, and never recorded as demand or as a gap: explaining a question is
not asking it.

empty_reason.description:
Set when nothing was found: `no_terms` (only function words),
`no_readable_collection` or `no_match`.

terms.description: The content terms, normalised and stemmed as the index stores them.

LockedField.description:
One field a business rule locks for the writer (D-789 §3.5): `effect` is
`hidden` or `disabled`. No value is ever echoed.

PaginatedResponse_CollectionCoverage.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

chunks_embedded.description:
Chunks carrying a vector from the configured model. `None` when
knowledge is lexical-only by configuration.

embedding_backlog.description:
Chunks still waiting for a vector from the configured model (never
embedded, or embedded by a different one). `None` when knowledge is
lexical-only by configuration.

items_draft.description: Items waiting in the draft review queue. Never chunked (D-489).

items_total.description: Live items in the collection, whatever their lifecycle.

last_indexed_at.description: The newest `indexed_at` among those chunks; `None` when there are none.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_GapTopic.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

items.description:
A row of the authors' knowledge-gap queue (D-452; surfaced by D-489).

The phrase is the scrubbed topic, never the caller's raw question — read
[`normalize_gap_phrase`]'s doc before widening anything here, and D-452
before changing what a row stores.

addressed_item_ref.description:
The Knowledge Base item that addressed this gap (D-489, migration
0300). No FK: the target is a runtime-provisioned entity table.

addressed_page_ref.description: The content page that addressed this gap, from the 0263 shape.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_GraphNode.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_KnowledgeCitation.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

items.description:
One passage returned from the knowledge corpus, with everything a citation
needs to resolve (`P-knowledge-base` §8, §11).

Every field is captured at projection time or computed here, never
reconstructed from the article at render time: an item edited after the
answer was generated would otherwise produce a citation pointing at a
heading that no longer exists.

data_source_id.description:
The Data Source that permissioned it — the collection `readable_collections`
resolved for this caller before the query ran.

fetched_at.description: When a web-sourced chunk was fetched. `None` for authored articles.

heading_path.description:
The heading path captured when the chunk was written, outermost first.
Empty for an article's lede, which precedes any heading.

item_id.description: The article record the passage came from.

passage.description: The enclosing section, not the matched chunk. See `expand`'s doc.

stale.description:
Past its `review_by` date. Computed server-side from a plain DATE
comparison, and it reaches a prompt only as untrusted context.

truncated.description:
The section exceeded the passage ceiling and was returned in part.
Reported so an answer can say so rather than presenting a fragment as
the whole.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_SearchPin.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

query_norm.description: The normalised query the pin answers.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_SearchStopword.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_SearchSynonym.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_SimilarPassage.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

entity_logicalname.description: The record the passage belongs to.

heading_path.description: The headings above the passage, outermost first.

page.description: For a document's PDF, the one-based page the passage is on.

score.description: One minus the cosine distance to the source; higher is nearer.

source_entity.description: Where it came from: the record itself, or a document attached to it.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

paths.description:
The shortest connections first, each the edges from `from` to `to`
in walking order (an edge may be walked against its direction).

truncated.description:
The walk from `from` hit a bound; a longer or wider connection may
exist.

page_ids.description:
Neighbor page ids, nearest first. Empty on a deployment where no
chunk has an embedding yet (D-452) — Stage 2's backfill is what
populates `knowledge_chunk.embedding`; this route does not
depend on anything else that is unbuilt.

RuleFailure.description:
One business-rule `error` policy that fired (D-789 §3.3), inside a
`rule_violation` body's `details.rules`. Carries names and the rule's own
message, never a record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RuleViolationDetails.description:
`details` of a `rule_violation` response (D-789): the field of the first
failing policy, when it names one, and every blocking `error` policy that
fired, the first (by rule display order) being the one `rule_id` names.

ScoreParts.description: How one result came to its score.

fused.description: The fused rank score from the legs, before any tuning.

legs.description: The legs that matched, with the fused statement's per-leg values.

opened.description: Added because the caller opened it from a search lately.

owner.description: Added because the caller owns the record.

pinned.description: Placed by a pin for this query.

score.description: The score shown: `fused + boost_added + owner + opened + team`.

synonyms.description: The synonyms the query also ran with.

team.description: Added because a team of the caller's owns it.

SearchDrainBacklog.description: A25-T5: how far the drain is behind.

events.description:
Events after this consumer's cursor, counted up to
[`attome_core::change_feed::LAG_COUNT_CAP`].

lag_seconds.description: Age of the oldest of them in seconds; 0 with nothing to read.

row_version.description: 0 while the entity has never been set.

attributes.description: Replaces every attribute setting of the entity.

SearchFacets.description:
A25-T9: the results counted by entity, owner (user id) and the month
they last changed (`YYYY-MM`), over every result the caller may see, not
only the page; the most common 20 of each.

oneOf.description: A25-T4: how the score came about, when asked for and allowed.

matched_legs.description:
Which legs matched this row. Useful to a human debugging relevance and
to the impression log's feature vector.

page.description:
A25-T6: for a document, the page of its file (a PDF) the query best
matches, one-based, so the file opens there.

bytes.description: The index table with its indexes, in bytes.

query_norm.description: The normalised query the pin answers.

query.description: The query, as people type it; it is normalised.

oneOf.description: A25-T7: what asking in words did, for `mode=ask`.

degraded.description:
Legs that did not run to completion. **Reported, never swallowed** — a
result set silently missing a leg looks like "no more matches", which
is indistinguishable from a correct empty answer.

oneOf.description: A25-T9: the facets, when asked for.

impression_id.description:
The handle a later interaction is reported against (TODO-021). `None`
when the impression could not be logged, which must not fail the
search.

limited.description:
AB5-T5: the index was down, so this is a short prefix match on each
readable entity's title from the database (route `fallback`), not a
ranked search. Sent only when true.

route.description:
Which route the query took. Exposed deliberately: "why did this query
return that" is the single most common search support question, and the
answer is almost always the route.

oneOf.description:
Set when the query was routed away from retrieval — an aggregation
question, which retrieval answers badly (see `router::Route`).

SearchStatus.description: A25-T5: how far the index is behind, and its size per entity.

sizes.description: Per entity, largest first, from the daily upkeep.

entity_logicalname.description:
For `"entity"`: the entity to route to. For `"saved_search"`: always
`"saved_search"` — pair with `record_id` to call `run`.

terms.description: 2 to 20 terms that mean the same.

SimilarRecord.description: A record to find passages like.

entity.description: The entity's logical name; `attome_document` for a file.

image.description:
Images like this one: a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF of at most 5 MB, as
base64 or a `data:` URL. 503 without an image-text model.

images.description:
Find images instead of passages: the images a `text` describes, or
those like a document's image named as `record`. Implied by `image`.

limit.description: Passages to return, 1 to 50; 10 when absent.

oneOf.description: Passages like this record's text, or like this document's file.

text.description: Passages like this description (at most 4,000 characters).

oneOf.description: The match set was bounded, so this is the real number.

The match set hit the candidate ceiling. There are at least this many;
counting the rest would cost a second full-predicate pass.

edge_types.description:
Restricts which edges the walk follows — `"lookup:{field}"`,
`"hierarchy:{field}"`, `"relationship:{type}"`, or the bare
`"relationship"` to admit every relationship type. `None` (the
default) follows everything the caller can see.

truncated.description:
Set whenever a bound (depth, per-hop fan-out, the overall node cap, or
the statement timeout) cut the walk short. Never silently return a
partial graph.

addressed_item_ref.description:
The Knowledge Base item that answers this gap. Written only when
`status = "addressed"`; ignored otherwise.

Warning.description:
Something the server did that the caller should know about though the
request succeeded (a value truncated, a default applied, a page clamped):
a stable `code` and English `message`. Sent only when there is one.

portal_session.name: __Secure-wp_{portal}_session
portal_session.description: A web portal user's session cookie, issued by the portal's sign-in; `{portal}` is the portal's keyword (`wp_{portal}_session` on plain-http local dev). Valid only on that portal's own routes.

s2s_hmac.name: x-s2s-signature
s2s_hmac.description: A system-to-system call, signed. Send `x-s2s-client-id`, `x-s2s-key-id`, `x-s2s-timestamp` (Unix milliseconds, within 300 seconds of the server's clock), `x-s2s-nonce` (single use: a repeat is refused) and `x-s2s-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the hex-decoded client secret, of `METHOD`, `PATH_AND_QUERY`, the hex SHA-256 of the body, `TIMESTAMP` and `NONCE`, joined by newlines in that order.

session_cookie.name: __Host-session_token
session_cookie.description: Browser session cookie issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Mutating requests additionally require the CSRF conditions enforced by `middleware::csrf`.
